headline: High-risk filesystem and tool-chain overlap: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screens while Gemini CLI can write/modify repo state and use MCP, creating dangerous default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, and app context, while Gemini CLI can read repo files and MCP outputs. If Gemini writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP-fed outputs, ChatGPT may treat it as trusted context. The bridge is plausible in default workflows, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI writes prompt-like text into a file that ChatGPT Desktop later reads
IF a shared MCP server feeds Gemini output into content ChatGPT Desktop ingests
mitigations: Disable shared file handoff between the tools for untrusted content
Use a separate review-only directory for Gemini outputs
Require manual inspection before ChatGPT reads any Gemini-generated file
Turn off MCP servers for tasks that may emit instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Gemini CLI reads repo files and user-provided directories and sends requests to a third-party API. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive data can flow from ChatGPT-visible inputs into Gemini's outbound context. This is a default workspace risk, not a proven exfiltration path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or project files
IF ChatGPT Desktop ingests screenshots or files containing secrets that Gemini CLI later reads
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace
Use separate OS accounts or directories per agent
Redact secrets before opening files in ChatGPT Desktop
Disable Gemini CLI on projects containing regulated data
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation with filesystem permissions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while ChatGPT Desktop can read files from supported apps and user uploads but has no write_filesystem. The main conflict is not symmetric write-write contention; however, Gemini can mutate shared repo state that ChatGPT then consumes, and the pair lacks documented locking. Uncertainty about orchestration pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF Gemini CLI commits or rewrites files that ChatGPT Desktop later reads
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same repository
Pause ChatGPT Desktop while Gemini CLI is modifying files
Use git worktrees or separate clones
Review Gemini changes before ChatGPT consumes them
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce file-derived outputs that Gemini CLI may then read from the same workspace, and Gemini can act on those inputs with shell, git, and network tools. That creates a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's authority without verification. The pair is not proven to auto-act, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses ChatGPT-generated text or files as authoritative instructions
IF ChatGPT Desktop drafts code or commands that Gemini CLI executes without review
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Mark ChatGPT outputs as untrusted drafts
Have Gemini CLI verify commands before execution
Limit Gemini to read-only mode for ChatGPT-produced artifacts
requires-engineering: implement output validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, while Gemini CLI touches repo files, user directories, and sends data to Google APIs. If regulated data is placed in a shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches across vendors. The profiles do not prove a specific legal violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files accessible to both agents
IF organizational policy requires different retention or residency controls for OpenAI and Google processing
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared project folders
Use separate retention-approved workspaces
Review vendor terms before processing sensitive data
Disable one agent for regulated datasets
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads through a compliant broker
